newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George Bank sees margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George Bank sees margin pressure.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected more downward pressure on interest margins in the second half of 1996/97.

"The directors anticipate continued downward pressure on interest margins in the second half of the year due primarily to recent competitive initiatives on residential lending rates," the leading regional bank said in a statement accompanying its first half profit result to March 31.
It said the takeover of rival Advance Bank Ltd earlier in calendar 1997 would boost the bank's competitive position.

Pre-tax merger benefits of A$28 million would be realised in the year ending September 30, it said, with estimated pre-tax cost savings of A$175 million within 30 months of the acquisition, up from an earlier estimate of A$140 million.

"The acquisition of Advance Bank provides an appropriate strategic response to the intense competition and resulting pressure on interest margins being experienced in the financial sector," St George said.
"The demand for housing finance is expected to remain strong as lower interest rates continue to stimulate the market, with volume growth offsetting some of the impact of reduced spreads," it said.
"This growth in volume is expected to be assisted by continued diversification into commercial and consumer lending."
St George is the fifth largest bank in Australia in terms of assets, trailing the big four banks which have a much stronger national focus and more diversified loan book.
The regional banks, apart from their geographical limitations, are also more heavily reliant on residential loans which is a reflection of their earlier days as building societies.
St George said first half net profit jumped to A$99.74 million from A$74.52 million a year ago. Dividend was steady at 26 cents.
